frequency_question: What proportion of major OFAC enforcement actions against foreign banks are initiated and executed within a 28-day preparation and announcement cycle from the final decision point?
membership_rule: Includes formal designation and financial prohibition actions by OFAC against Tier-1 foreign commercial entities; excludes minor warning letters or settlement discussions without immediate designation.

cases.name: Bank of China subpoena enforcement / related actions

provenance_note: rate of 0% from only 4 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: Exhaustive review of major foreign bank sanctions execution timelines shows none executed within a 28-day total elapsed window from zero-base.
known_gaps: Classified internal emergency actions are not part of the public registry, though procedural constraints remain bound by federal rulemaking and inter-agency notification laws.
skeleton: Complex regulatory investigations require inter-agency review (State, Treasury, NSC), legal drafting, intelligence vetting, and diplomatic notification, creating a minimum irreducible procedural path length.
multiplier: Inter-agency review (30-90 days) + Legal sufficiency review (15-30 days) + Diplomatic/counterparty notification buffer (15-30 days) = Minimum procedural time 60 to 150 days.
validity_reason: Administrative Procedure Act and inter-agency coordination statutes remain stable over medium-term horizons.
